  <text id="90:26" name="Scattered rewards Travelers accumulate points across credit cards, airlines, and hotels without a clear view of what they can unlock together." x="736" y="1835" width="584" height="81" />
  <text id="143:7" name="The Strategic Optimizer Knows the system and works to maximize value." x="426" y="3958" width="250" height="78" />
  <text id="143:8" name="The Aspirational Expert Understands the basics and wants value, but needs guidance." x="735" y="3958" width="243" height="104" />
  <text id="143:9" name="The Casual Redeemer Uses points sporadically and prioritizes ease." x="1038" y="3958" width="255" height="78" />
  <text id="123:17" name="Point.ly began as a startup concept from a United Airlines manager who wanted to give travelers one view of their rewards. Travelers face three problems:" x="734" y="1737" width="586" height="78" />
  <text id="137:3" name="I interviewed 10 travelers to understand how they managed rewards, evaluated redemption value, and navigated decisions around transfers and group travel." x="428" y="2636" width="865" height="57" />
  <text id="123:5" name="Turning fragmented loyalty points into new travel possibilities " x="734" y="203" width="547" height="89" />
  <text id="123:8" name="UX@Berkeley project team" x="734" y="292" width="490" height="22" />
  <text id="90:27" name="Finding the best redemption requires expertise Comparing cash, points, transfer partners, and booking portals means navigating different values, rules, and systems." x="736" y="1936" width="584" height="81" />
  <text id="90:28" name="Groups can’t pool rewards Friends may have significant rewards collectively, but few tools show what becomes possible when their points are considered together." x="736" y="2037" width="584" height="81" />

  <text id="136:61" name="“The bank portals feel like Expedia from 2010. It’s hard to know if I’m getting a good deal.”" x="465" y="2775" width="207" height="96" />
  <text id="136:81" name="“I want to plan trips with friends, but it’s so hard to coordinate and share options together.”" x="1072" y="2775" width="215" height="189" />
  <text id="136:60" name="Isa  Tech Worker, 30s " x="483" y="3058" width="170" height="66" />

  <text id="136:73" name="“I want a single view of all my points so I don’t have to log into multiple accounts.”" x="897" y="3307" width="368" height="251" />
  <text id="136:71" name="Daniel Student, 20s " x="539" y="3489" width="170" height="66" />
  <rounded-rectangle id="136:52" name="Concerned man holding phone with account tiles-4 1" x="322" y="3135" width="614" height="409" />

  <text id="136:82" name="Jasmine, 30s " x="793" y="3058" width="170" height="66" />
  <text id="136:79" name="“It’s hard to understand the real value of a points transfer — will I actually save money?”" x="775" y="2775" width="207" height="96" />
  <text id="138:94" name="Users did not necessarily need more ways to earn points. They needed help understanding the value already sitting in their wallets." x="735" y="3649" width="535" height="140" />

  <text id="143:74" name="We analyzed existing rewards platforms to understand competitors’ unique differentiating features" x="427" y="4362" width="822" height="22" />
  <text id="163:9" name="We mapped each competitors’ features and user flows to identify strengths, friction points, and opportunities" x="427" y="4996" width="893" height="22" />
  <text id="163:14" name="Guided by our research, we quickly explored multiple concepts, including a Chrome extension, centralized rewards wallet, AI trip planning, itinerary comparison, and personalized points recommendations." x="427" y="6396" width="884" height="52" />
  <text id="187:4" name="We prioritized the concepts that most directly addressed our research findings: consolidating rewards, simplifying comparisons, and making redemption opportunities actionable. Broader ideas that moved beyond these core needs were deprioritized." x="427" y="6995" width="856" height="78" />
  <text id="314:31" name="I developed Point.ly’s visual identity to make the complexity of credit card points feel clear and approachable, balancing a friendly personality with the credibility of a financial tool." x="427" y="7588" width="856" height="52" />
  <text id="316:43" name="We translated our research into a high-fidelity MVP prototype focused on consolidating rewards, comparing redemption options, and guiding travelers toward booking. The project remained at the prototype stage." x="427" y="8225" width="856" height="52" />
  <text id="145:135" name="Text" x="427" y="5559" width="822" height="26" />
  <text id="145:102" name="Broad multi-program search for quickly finding award availability." x="676" y="4493" width="555" height="18" />
  <text id="145:103" name="Flight and hotel award search with strong free tools." x="676" y="4553" width="555" height="18" />
  <text id="145:104" name="Guided award search with step-by-step booking support." x="676" y="4434" width="649" height="18" />
  <text id="145:106" name="Hotel-focused award availability and redemption alerts." x="676" y="4670" width="458" height="18" />
  <text id="145:107" name="Centralized tracking for points balances and expirations." x="676" y="4729" width="452" height="18" />
  <text id="145:109" name="Flexible award search with filters and trend data." x="676" y="4611" width="402" height="18" />
  <text id="145:110" name="Educational content, points valuations, and credit-card guidance." x="676" y="4788" width="474" height="18" />
  <text id="145:129" name="Powerful, fast award search designed for experienced users." x="676" y="4847" width="474" height="18" />
  <rounded-rectangle id="348:3" name="Points Box" x="883" y="5552" width="439" height="249" />
  <rounded-rectangle id="348:10" name="Points Box" x="883" y="5818" width="439" height="249" />
  <rounded-rectangle id="348:14" name="Points Box" x="428" y="5818" width="439" height="249" />
  <rounded-rectangle id="348:6" name="Points Box" x="426" y="5552" width="439" height="249" />
  <text id="145:138" name="Savvy travelers knew the transfer partners and redemption tricks. Everyone else had the same options but no easy way to find them. " x="1000" y="5646" width="296" height="91" />
  <text id="348:11" name="Instead of a flat “not enough points,” provide a list of creative ways to close the gap, such as current promos and affiliated points programs. " x="1000" y="5911" width="269" height="91" />
  <text id="348:15" name="For people planning together, looking at combined resources rather than individual balances could open travel options" x="545" y="5911" width="269" height="91" />
  <text id="348:7" name="Knowing you have 80,000 points is meaningless unless you know what they can buy and whether transferring is worth it. " x="543" y="5651" width="281" height="91" />
  <text id="348:5" name="Insight: Expertise created  an uneven playing field" x="1000" y="5588" width="296" height="48" />
  <text id="348:12" name="Opportunity: Provide ideas to  close points gaps fast" x="1000" y="5853" width="296" height="48" />

  <text id="314:36" name="Interviewing travelers with different habits and levels of points experience taught me that people can approach the same problem differently but still need similar things from a product.  At the hackathon, I turned our findings into a PRD, used AI coding tools to build a working prototype, and tested it with users. This helped me connect what I heard in interviews to specific choices about how the product should work.  The biggest lesson came from working through the full process: listening to a full spectrum of user experiences, making sense of what I heard, building, testing, and improving the design based on feedback." x="736" y="9849" width="492" height="301" />
